classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught algebraic parity test and connect each conclusion to symmetry in a graph, retaining the rational functions' excluded inputs.

content.prompt:
Decide whether these functions are odd, even, or neither.
Check your answer by sketching the curve on DESMOS.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\frac{(-x)^3}{(-x)^4-(-x)^2}\\&=\frac{-x^3}{x^4-x^2}\\&=-f(x)\end{align*}$$
The domain excludes $-1,0,1$ and is symmetric about zero. The function is odd. The DESMOS graph has rotational symmetry about the origin, including its hole at the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\frac{1}{(-x)^3-1}\\&=\frac{1}{-x^3-1}\\&=-\frac{1}{x^3+1}\end{align*}$$
This equals neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ identically. The function is neither odd nor even. The DESMOS graph has neither symmetry about the $y$-axis nor rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\frac{3}{(-x)^2-4}\\&=\frac{3}{x^2-4}\\&=f(x)\end{align*}$$
The domain excludes $-2,2$ and is symmetric about zero. The function is even. The DESMOS graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\frac{-x-3}{-x+3}\\&=\frac{x+3}{x-3}\end{align*}$$
This equals neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ identically. The function is neither odd nor even. The DESMOS graph has neither symmetry about the $y$-axis nor rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\frac{(-x)^3}{(-x)^5-(-x)^2}\\&=\frac{-x^3}{-x^5-x^2}\\&=\frac{x^3}{x^5+x^2}\end{align*}$$
This equals neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ identically. The function is neither odd nor even. The DESMOS graph has neither symmetry about the $y$-axis nor rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=(-x-2)^2\\&=(x+2)^2\end{align*}$$
This equals neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ identically. The function is neither odd nor even. The DESMOS graph is symmetric about $x=2$, rather than the $y$-axis, and has no rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=3^{-x}-3^x\\&=-(3^x-3^{-x})\\&=-f(x)\end{align*}$$
The function is odd. The DESMOS graph has rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=3^{-x}+3^x\\&=3^x+3^{-x}\\&=f(x)\end{align*}$$
The function is even. The DESMOS graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=3^{-x}+(-x)^3\\&=3^{-x}-x^3\end{align*}$$
This equals neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ identically. The function is neither odd nor even. The DESMOS graph has neither symmetry about the $y$-axis nor rotational symmetry about the origin.
